callable.name: compare
callable.unknown_mode: false; never fall back to permissive equality

case_field: output_comparison is optional; absent/null selects exact structural comparison. Rules are public requirement semantics, not intended-identity hints.

input_shape.args: array of ordered positional JSON values

example_adapter.policy: Add compare only in a derived host-judge request. Do not edit authored examples. Apply identical rules to public and private checks. Compare-mode assignment is fixed before candidate opening.
example_adapter.sandbox_boundary: Only invocation inputs and returned program enter sandbox execution. Expected values and comparator code remain in host judge.
example_adapter.private_boundary: Private checks execute only after route response capture; never used for ranking, repair or generation.

requirements: Recursive JSON structure and ordered lists match.
Booleans are never numbers; integer expected values require integer actual values.
Finite numeric outputs use numerical equality when expected type is noninteger number.

modes.authored_rule: numeric lists with absolute or relative tolerance 1e-5
requirements: Both outputs are flat lists of equal length.
Elements must be finite numbers, never booleans.
Preserve order. For each pair, absolute difference must be <= max(1e-5,1e-5*max(abs(actual),abs(expected))).
Both outputs are lists containing integers, never booleans.
Each list has no duplicate values.
Compare sorted lists, retaining length and multiplicity checks.

modes.authored_rule: unordered outer list; preserve inner order
requirements: Both outputs are lists of integer lists; booleans are invalid.
Each full inner sequence must be unique in the outer list.
Outer order may change; inner order cannot change.
Compare sorted tuples of complete rows with length and duplicate checks; never convert only to sets.

modes.authored_rule: exact rational decimal equivalence; parentheses denote indefinite repetition; enforce requested sign/integer/no-exponent formatting
requirements: Both outputs are strings encoding decimal numbers with optional minus sign, optional decimal part, and optional final parenthesized repeating digits.
No exponent, plus sign, redundant integer leading zeros, negative zero, or empty fractional part.
An integer result must have no decimal point. Terminating decimals must not be encoded using repeating blocks.

Parse exactly with integer arithmetic. For integer part I, nonrepeating digits F of length m, and repeating digits R of length k, magnitude is I + F/10^m + R/(10^m*(10^k-1)); omit terms not present and apply sign.
Equivalent nonterminating representations are accepted without float conversion; equality is exact rational equality.

representation: JSON positional arguments only; no pointer objects or custom typed markers are needed.
